input.symptom: PC gets an IP address but cannot reach the server in VLAN 30. The PC can ping its default gateway.
input.topology_note: PC connected to Switch1 Fa0/2 (VLAN 10). Switch1 trunk to Router1 Fa0/0. Server in VLAN 30 on Switch1 Fa0/5.
input.show_output:
show vlan brief
VLAN Name Status Ports
10 Data active Fa0/2
30 Servers active Fa0/5

switchport access vlan 30 command missing on Fa0/5 - port shows VLAN 1
show interfaces trunk
Port Mode Encapsulation Status Native vlan
Fa0/1 on 802.1q trunking 1

issues.evidence: Port is still associated with default VLAN 1 instead of the intended VLAN.
issues.recommendation: Apply 'switchport access vlan <id>' on the port to assign the correct VLAN.

ai_result.root_cause: Wrong VLAN assignment - a switch port is in the wrong VLAN or the VLAN is not carried across the link.
evidence: The switch output shows the port still in VLAN 1 (default VLAN).
The output notes that 'switchport access vlan 30' is missing on the server port.
Rule checker flagged: Missing VLAN Assignment (Medium).
fix_steps: Find the affected switch port.
Assign it to the correct VLAN with 'switchport access vlan <id>'.
Check the VLAN again with 'show vlan brief'.
Test connectivity from the affected host.

input.symptom: Internal users cannot reach the internet even though the NAT and ACL rules look correct on paper.
input.topology_note: ACL 101 meant to filter outbound internet traffic on Serial0/1/0.
input.show_output:
show run interface Serial0/1/0
ip access-group 101 in
(ACL 101 was designed for traffic leaving the router, should be applied 'out' or reversed)

issues.evidence: ACL is applied in the wrong direction ('in' vs 'out') relative to the traffic it should filter.
issues.recommendation: Re-apply the access-group in the correct direction on the interface.

ai_result.root_cause: Access control list (ACL) problem - the ACL is blocking the wrong traffic or filtering the wrong range.
evidence: The ACL is applied inbound on the interface it filters.
Rule checker flagged: ACL Applied in Wrong Direction (High).
fix_steps: Review the ACL for overly broad deny statements.
Confirm the ACL is on the correct interface and direction.
Correct the wildcard mask if needed.

input.symptom: Wi-Fi in the office is connected but extremely slow and drops frequently during business hours.
input.topology_note: Three APs (AP1, AP2, AP3) cover adjacent areas of the same floor.
input.show_output:
AP1 channel: 6
AP2 channel: 6
AP3 channel: 6
(all APs using the same 2.4GHz channel, high co-channel interference)

issues.evidence: Multiple access points are configured on the same channel.
issues.recommendation: Configure adjacent APs on non-overlapping channels (e.g. 1, 6, 11).

ai_result.root_cause: Wireless problem - Wi-Fi association or coverage configuration is wrong.
evidence: Multiple access points are using the same channel (co-channel interference).
Rule checker flagged: Wireless Channel Overlap (Low).
fix_steps: Match the client security profile to the AP security settings.
Re-enable SSID broadcast if clients must see the network.
Use non-overlapping channels on nearby access points.
verification_steps: Reconnect the client and confirm association

input.symptom: PCs in VLAN 20 can ping each other but cannot reach their default gateway or any other subnet.
input.topology_note: VLAN 20 subnet is 192.168.20.0/24. Router1 SVI Vlan20 is 192.168.20.1.
input.show_output:
ipconfig /all
IPv4 Address: 192.168.20.10
Subnet Mask: 255.255.255.0
Default Gateway: 192.168.30.1
Router1 show ip interface brief -> Vlan20 192.168.20.1 up up

issues.evidence: Host IP (192.168.20.10) and default gateway (192.168.30.1) are on different /24 subnets.
issues.recommendation: Correct the default gateway so it resides on the same subnet as the host, or fix the host's IP/mask configuration.

ai_result.root_cause: Default gateway problem - the host's gateway does not match the router address for its subnet.
evidence: The configured default gateway does not match the router SVI for the host's subnet.
The host (192.168.20.10) and its default gateway (192.168.30.1) are on different /24 subnets.
Rule checker flagged: Gateway Mismatch (High).
fix_steps: Confirm the correct gateway IP for the host's subnet.
Update the host's default gateway (static config or DHCP).
Renew the host's IP configuration if it uses DHCP.
Ping the gateway to confirm.

input.symptom: During peak hours, some internal users lose internet access while others remain connected.
input.topology_note: Router1 uses a NAT pool (not overload) for translating internal addresses.
input.show_output:
show ip nat statistics
Total active translations: 20 (20 static, 0 dynamic; 0 extended)
Pool NAT-POOL: netmask 255.255.255.240
 start 203.0.113.10 end 203.0.113.20
 total addresses 11 allocated 11 (100%) misses 47

issues.evidence: A non-standard or mismatched subnet mask was found relative to the expected network size.
issues.recommendation: Correct the mask on the host or interface so it matches the rest of the VLAN/subnet.

issues.evidence: The NAT pool is fully allocated (all addresses in use).
issues.recommendation: Increase the pool size or switch to PAT/overload to share addresses.

ai_result.root_cause: NAT problem - address translation is not working as expected.
evidence: The NAT pool is fully allocated (11/11, 100%).
Rule checker flagged: Incorrect Subnet Mask (High).
Rule checker flagged: NAT Pool Exhausted (Medium).
fix_steps: Confirm 'ip nat inside' / 'ip nat outside' on the correct interfaces.
Check the NAT pool size against the number of hosts.
Remove duplicate static NAT mappings.

input.symptom: Inter-VLAN routing fails for VLAN 30 only; VLAN 10 and VLAN 20 route correctly.
input.topology_note: Router1 Gi0/0 has subinterfaces Gi0/0.10, Gi0/0.20, Gi0/0.30 for router-on-a-stick.
input.show_output:
show run interface Gi0/0.30
encapsulation dot1Q 3
ip address 192.168.30.1 255.255.255.0

issues.evidence: Subinterface gi0/0.30 is tagging frames with dot1Q 3 instead of 30.
issues.recommendation: Correct the encapsulation under the subinterface to match its VLAN: 'encapsulation dot1Q <expected-vlan>'.

ai_result.root_cause: Routing problem - a route or a routing-related interface is missing or misconfigured.
evidence: Subinterface 30 is tagging frames with dot1Q 3 instead of dot1Q 30.
Rule checker flagged: Incorrect dot1Q Tag (High).
fix_steps: Check whether the destination subnet appears in 'show ip route'.
Add the missing route or fix the routing protocol / interface.
Confirm the affected interface is up.

input.symptom: Users can ping the web server by IP address but cannot browse to it using its hostname.
input.topology_note: PC on VLAN 10, DNS server configured as 8.8.8.8 in the DHCP scope but internal DNS is 192.168.10.5.

ipconfig /all
DNS Servers: 8.8.8.8
nslookup intranet.local
*** 8.8.8.8 can't find intranet.local: Non-existent domain

issues.evidence: Hostname resolution fails (non-existent domain) even though access by IP address works.
issues.recommendation: Point the client at the correct internal DNS server and verify Layer 3 reachability to it.

ai_result.root_cause: DNS problem - hostname resolution is failing.
evidence: The DNS lookup fails with 'non-existent domain', but IP-based access works.
The configured DNS server cannot resolve the internal hostname.
Rule checker flagged: DNS Resolution Failure (Medium).
fix_steps: Confirm the correct internal DNS server address.
Point the DHCP scope (or static config) at the right DNS server.
Verify Layer 3 reachability to the DNS server.
